topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out the core learning objectives concerning cancer treatment modalities.

topics.label: Surgical and radiation approaches to localized tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the fundamental difficulty of selective cancer cell killing and the clinical application of surgery and radiotherapy to eradicate localized tumors.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy and drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms, toxicities, and efflux pump-mediated resistance associated with conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how therapeutic strategies can selectively target tumor cell vulnerabilities resulting from hormone dependence, defective checkpoints, and impaired DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogenic kinase inhibitors and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the targeted inhibition of hyperactive oncogenic kinases and the molecular pathways driving resistance and drug addiction to these inhibitors.

topics.label: Antibody-based cancer therapeutics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates specifically recognize cell surface markers to eliminate tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell targeting
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and therapeutic strategies that harness or engineer T cells to destroy cancer cells.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the systemic challenges, clinical survival improvements, and future paradigms in cancer detection and treatment.
